intro: The gaslight in 221B guttered low, as if the room itself were holding its breath, and the detective was gone—only his violin sat on the chair, one string wound tight to a note that was not quite true, and beside it a stack of notes tied with a fraying ribbon, each addressed to whoever might be clever enough to read between the lines. The Irregulars drifted in and out like smoke, each pocketing a scrap, each coming back with half a truth and a shrug, but the one who pieced the scraps together always left a single odd stitch in the telling, a word that did not belong to the story but slipped in anyway, as though the telling itself had taken up a habit of hiding things in plain sight. Mrs Hudson tutted and swept the hearth, muttering that Holmes had never been much good at leaving instructions, only at leaving things that almost said enough. A cold wind rattled the sash and the violin sang, faintly, one string at a time.
echo: When you have eliminated the impossible, whatever remains is the answer.
